SOC 2 Type 2 Report

Acme Cloud Services, Inc.

Report on Acme Cloud Services, Inc.'s Description of Its Cloud Hosting
Platform and on the Suitability of the Design and Operating Effectiveness
of Its Controls Relevant to Security, Availability, and Confidentiality

For the period January 1, 2026 to June 30, 2026

Prepared by: Smith & Patel LLP

THIS IS A FAKE REPORT CREATED FOR SOFTWARE TESTING. IT DESCRIBES NO REAL
COMPANY OR AUDIT FIRM.
=== PAGE BREAK ===
Section 1: Independent Service Auditor's Report

To: Management of Acme Cloud Services, Inc.

Scope

We have examined Acme Cloud Services, Inc.'s ("Acme" or the "service
organization") accompanying description of its Cloud Hosting Platform
(the "system") throughout the period January 1, 2026 to June 30, 2026
(the "description"), and the suitability of the design and operating
effectiveness of controls stated in the description throughout the period
January 1, 2026 to June 30, 2026, to provide reasonable assurance that
Acme's service commitments and system requirements were achieved based on
the trust services criteria relevant to Security, Availability, and
Confidentiality (applicable trust services criteria) set forth in TSP
section 100, 2017 Trust Services Criteria for Security, Availability,
Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, and Privacy.

Acme uses a subservice organization, Amazon Web Services, Inc. (AWS), to
provide data center hosting services. The description indicates that
complementary subservice organization controls that are suitably designed
and operating effectively are necessary, along with controls at Acme, to
achieve Acme's service commitments. The description presents Acme's
controls and the types of complementary subservice organization controls
assumed in the design of Acme's controls. The description does not
disclose the actual controls at the subservice organization. Our
examination did not include the services provided by the subservice
organization, and we have not evaluated the suitability of the design or
operating effectiveness of such complementary subservice organization
controls.

The description indicates that complementary user entity controls that are
suitably designed and operating effectively are necessary, along with
controls at Acme, to achieve Acme's service commitments and system
requirements. Our examination did not include such complementary user
entity controls.
=== PAGE BREAK ===
Section 1: Independent Service Auditor's Report (continued)

Basis for Qualified Opinion

Acme states in its description that user access to production systems is
removed within one business day of termination. However, as noted on
page 7 of the description of tests of controls and results, for 4 of 25
terminated employees sampled, access to production systems was not removed
until between 6 and 21 days after termination. As a result, controls were
not operating effectively to provide reasonable assurance that Acme's
service commitments and system requirements were achieved based on
criterion CC6.2.

Qualified Opinion

In our opinion, except for the matter described in the Basis for Qualified
Opinion paragraph, in all material respects,

a. the description presents the Cloud Hosting Platform that was designed
   and implemented throughout the period January 1, 2026 to June 30, 2026,
   in accordance with the description criteria.

b. the controls stated in the description were suitably designed and
   operated effectively throughout the period January 1, 2026 to
   June 30, 2026, to provide reasonable assurance that Acme's service
   commitments and system requirements were achieved based on the
   applicable trust services criteria, if complementary subservice
   organization controls and complementary user entity controls assumed in
   the design of Acme's controls operated effectively throughout that
   period.

Smith & Patel LLP
Denver, Colorado
August 14, 2026

Section 2: Management's Assertion

We have prepared the accompanying description of Acme Cloud Services,
Inc.'s Cloud Hosting Platform throughout the period January 1, 2026 to
June 30, 2026, based on the criteria for a description of a service
organization's system set forth in DC section 200, 2018 Description
Criteria for a Description of a Service Organization's System in a SOC 2
Report.

We confirm, to the best of our knowledge and belief, that the controls
stated in the description were suitably designed and operated effectively
throughout the period, except for the matter described in the Basis for
Qualified Opinion paragraph of the independent service auditor's report.

Acme Cloud Services, Inc. Management
=== PAGE BREAK ===
Section 3: Description of the Cloud Hosting Platform

Subservice Organizations

Acme uses the carve-out method to present the following subservice
organization. The controls at the subservice organization are excluded
from the scope of this report.

Subservice Organization        Services Provided
Amazon Web Services, Inc.      Data center hosting, physical security,
                               and environmental protection

Complementary Subservice Organization Controls

Acme's controls are designed with the assumption that the following
controls are implemented by AWS:

CSOC-1  AWS is responsible for restricting physical access to data center
        facilities to authorized personnel.
CSOC-2  AWS is responsible for maintaining environmental protections,
        including fire suppression and power redundancy.
CSOC-3  AWS is responsible for monitoring and maintaining the hardware
        that supports the hosted infrastructure.
=== PAGE BREAK ===
Section 3: Description of the Cloud Hosting Platform (continued)

Complementary User Entity Controls

Acme's controls were designed with the assumption that certain controls
would be implemented by user entities. User entities should implement
the following controls:

CUEC-1  User entities are responsible for provisioning and removing their
        own users' access to the Acme customer portal.
CUEC-2  User entities are responsible for ensuring that their users keep
        their passwords and multi-factor authentication devices secure.
CUEC-3  User entities are responsible for reviewing the access of their
        users to the Acme platform at least quarterly.
CUEC-4  User entities are responsible for notifying Acme of security
        incidents involving their accounts in a timely manner.

=== PAGE BREAK ===
Section 5: Other Information Provided by Acme Cloud Services, Inc.

The information in this section is presented by management and has not
been subjected to the procedures applied in the examination.

Management's Response to Exceptions

CC6.2 - Management's response: Acme has implemented an automated
integration between the HR system and the identity provider so that
access is disabled automatically when a termination is recorded. The
integration went live on July 15, 2026.

CC8.1 - Management's response: The two changes were emergency fixes.
Acme has updated its change management procedure to require
retrospective approval within 24 hours for emergency changes and has
added a weekly report of unapproved changes.
